The highlighted word followed the playback time: "zero" at 0.66s, "one" at 1.37s, "two" at 2.78s, "three" at 3.48s and "four" at 4.88s. That happens because the page only updates when the browser sends its regular playback-time updates, which come every 250ms or so. Seeking to a new spot updates it too.

I didn't change any of the app's files; the test script was in `/tmp/capchk`.

It doesn't work. The first click on Load does nothing.

The click handler in `app.js` counts clicks and exits early on the first one (`if (clickCount === 1) return;`). "Loaded 3 items" only shows up on the second click. I confirmed this by firing the click from script: after one click the result was still empty, and after the second it read "Loaded 3 items".

One odd thing I didn't track down: the browser tool's real mouse clicks didn't reach the handler at all, and the count stayed at 0. The button isn't covered by anything, so that part may just be the tool. Either way, the early exit in the code means one click is never enough.

I didn't change any app files.

{"works": false, "cause": "The Load handler in app.js ignores the first click (`if (clickCount === 1) return;`), so \"Loaded 3 items\" only appears after a second click."}
